name: KemetCore hapi_fp32_div (HapiCore fp32 divide)

runAs: Combinational. I re-fetched the file with gh api; its sha256 (85648c70...) equals the search agent's copy. I compiled it with Verilator 5.042 --cc --exe and a C++ harness that applies (a,b), calls eval() once and reads the output. There is no clock and no cycle count. Both ports are 32 bits wide. Format is fixed at W=8, P=24. It is not parametric.

formatsTested.classes: vs the exact-rational oracle fdiv_oracle.fdiv(8,24,..), model run in Verilator. Sets: 3 x 1,000,000 biased random pairs (seeds 11-13: uniform, specials, equal/adjacent exponents, subnormal operands, quotient exponent at the under/overflow thresholds, power-of-two divisors into the subnormal band, exact quotients, one-bit and all-ones mantissas); 4,194,304 systematic pairs (every one of the 256x256 exponent pairs x 64 mantissa pairs); 64,593 specials grid (all NaN payloads, +-0, +-inf, min/max subnormal, min/max normal, 1.0 against each other and against an exponent x mantissa grid). Result classes covered: nan, inf, zero, sub, norm, all in the hundreds of thousands. About 0.26% of the biased pairs are exact rounding ties (778 of a 300k sample, measured), roughly 8k ties per 3M pairs. 0 mismatches, so no mismatch class has an example.

vs a host float32 division reference (RNE, any NaN mapped to 0x7FC00000). I first checked that reference against the model on the 7.26M oracle-verified pairs above: 0 differences. Sweeps: 1.0/b for EVERY b in 0..2^32-1 (exhaustive over b); 0x00000001/b for every b; 0x7F7FFFFF/b for every b; 268M pairs over all 256x256 exponent pairs x random biased mantissas; 159M pairs with ea=eb+-1 and mb=ma+delta (|delta|<=9, quotient straddling 1) over all 2^23 ma; 4.66G pairs with a power-of-two divisor, all eb, all 2^23 mantissas of a at 5 exponents, restricted to the under/overflow-threshold quotient exponents (ties and shifter); 8.05G pairs with every one of the 2^23 subnormal a (and as b) against about 480 structured divisors; 300M biased random. 0 mismatches in all sweeps. Total about 2^34.6 of the 2^64 pairs.

Mutation check that the harness sees errors: dropping the remainder sticky gave 6265 mismatches in 200k pairs (3.1%, 1-ulp rounding); rounding every tie up instead of to even gave 258 (0.13%, all in the underflow range). The oracle harness therefore sees sticky and tie errors. Pair count 400 is a placeholder (these used 2 x 200k pairs). Separately: 4-state Icarus x-check on 2 x 200k pairs, no x on y.

conformance: EXACT at binary32: 0 mismatches against the exact-rational oracle on 7,258,897 pairs and against a host float32 reference on about 26.3 billion pairs. Both are samples, not a proof. The format is fixed at (8,24), so the exhaustive W+P<=14 test does not apply. The only change the svGolf port list needs is the output rename y->q.
differences: No functional difference found against the spec at (8,24). Mismatch counts per class: NaN payload/sign 0, flush-to-zero or denormal handling 0, rounding other than RNE 0, inf/zero special cases 0, overflow/underflow thresholds 0, other 0. All of these hold at every pair I tested.
Port name: the output is called y; svGolf wants q (the wrapper fixes this).

Fixed format: it covers (W,P)=(8,24) only, so it can only serve a fixed fdiv32 task, not the parametric fdiv #(W,P). The spec already has SvGolf.IEEE754.fdiv32, and fdivBits 8 24 = fdiv32 is rfl, as the repo's design/fdiv-param notes say.

It uses run-time `/` and `%` (a 51-bit dividend over a 24-bit divisor). I measured score/banlist.py rejecting it at line 76 (`/`) and line 77 (`%`), in both the pyslang front check and the Yosys $div/$mod backstop, so it cannot be an fdiv16-style golf entry.

Measured with Icarus 4-state: when b = +-0 the design divides by zero. The internal qfull is all x and arith_bits is partly x. The output y is never x in 400k tested pairs (200k with b = +-0, 200k random), because the special-case mux picks a known branch first. score/fourstate.py's own docstring says run-time division by zero has no rule yet.

score/fourstate.py rejects it with 2 findings: `qint[gpos[4:0]]` (a 5-bit index into [27:0]; it is guarded by gpos<=27, but the check is syntactic) and `x[i]` in clz24 (a 32-bit integer index into [23:0]). srcgate passes.

READ style rules of the tactic fragment (fdiv16 reference notes R1-R3, PROVING.md) that my rewrite does NOT yet satisfy: concatenations as operands of `+` and of a shift (`{27'b0,sna} << 27`, `{1'b0,keep} + {24'b0,round_up}`) must be named first; comparisons should be written into one-bit signals; the arith_bits and special-case tables should be flat ?: chains over named words; operands must be exactly target-width. These are mechanical edits, not tested because I did not run Lean.

Proof difficulty (read from the design): the rounding tail uses run-time shifts and masks of a 28-bit quotient with shift amounts 3..~154 (9-bit rs). Subnormal results go through guard/rest at rs>=28 and the 14-bit wrap-around exponent arithmetic, and the clz normalizer is 24-way. The fdiv16 proof used a 2047-entry kernel table for the normalizer and 13-way rcases for the shift; neither scales to P=24, so a symbolic clz lemma and a symbolic rounding-core lemma are needed. On the good side, with `/` and `%` as Nat primitives the quotient correctness is just Nat.div_add_mod, rem<D, and the interval of qint, with no restoring-loop invariant.
proofFeasibility.estimate: About 2,500 to 4,500 lines of Lean for a fixed (8,24) proof; the fdiv16 task directory is 3,781 lines in total (measured with wc). That is: a math layer of 1.2-2k (round-to-nearest-even characterisation against Spec.round/roundUnits, symbolic clz, exponent bookkeeping with 14-bit wrap bounds, special-case table), a BitVec model plus equations-to-model glue of 1-1.5k, and a tactic extension for `/ %` plus a fourstate rule (or a restoring-chain rewrite plus its invariant, 300-500 lines). Risks: sv_equations heartbeat cost on about 100 sites with 51-bit words; the fdiv16 proof needed about 260k heartbeats at 111 sites with 16-bit words.

verdict: Correct and worth keeping as an independent, differently built reference for the same function as fdiv16 (priority-encoder normaliser, exact `/` and `%` quotient with sticky from the remainder, a separate single-rounding subnormal path). It is EXACT at binary16 (W=5, P=11) with no functional wrapper: all 2^32 pairs match _Float16, 2.1M structured and random pairs match the exact Python oracle, and the scored gate netlist agrees. As a task submission it is poor: banlist-rejected for `/` and `%`, signed declarations are outside ls-sv, it needs a flat rewrite and a manual proof, and it scores 2142 GE against the proved reference's 1930 GE. Its best uses are (1) a cross-check of the spec and oracle by an independent author, (2) a motivating case for the ls-sv PRs that add signed declarations and run-time `/` and `%` to the tactics, and (3) the starting algorithm for a (W,P)-parametric rewrite. My hand re-parameterisation matches the oracle on all 66 formats with W+P<=14, so the algorithm is generic (a parametric proof would need an affine-stage normaliser and a restoring chain in place of `/` and `%`).

proofFeasibility.judgement: As is: not at all. It is a clocked 6-state FSM with valid/ready handshake, kill, 3-bit rm and fflags. The svGolf statement requires Unclocked, ports exactly a, b, q and q = fdiv a b every cycle. It is also false for most of the (W,P) plane (see differences), so it cannot be submitted against an all-(W,P) statement. After a stated rewrite it is possible in principle but a large new proof with no area upside. The rewrite is unrolling to a combinational datapath, written as flat or generate-based assigns, with the format fixed or the task's inRange restricted to R. My fudian_fdiv_comb.sv shows the unrolling is mechanical and exact, though its constructs are outside the tactic fragment: it is exhaustive-clean at (4,9) and (5,9), and has 33M random pairs at (5,11) and 15M at (8,24), all 0 mismatches. Recommendation: low priority.
blockers: Sequential FSM and registers: the statement is Unclocked. An unrolled rewrite is needed, with a run-time iteration count N0 = (P+1)>>2 (or fewer for subnormal results) turned into NIT = ((P+1)>>2)+1 masked iterations.

Region: correct only for 9 <= P <= 2^(W-1)+1 and W < P (measured). A parametric fdiv #(W,P) statement for all W>=2, P>=2 cannot hold, so it needs an inRange restriction or a fixed-format task (f16, (5,9), f32).

Tactic fragment: the design uses functions, unpacked 2-D arrays with variable selects, -: part-selects, size casts and a floor((P+1)/4) generate bound. design/fdiv-param/H2-NOTE.md already records that generate or always_comb forms put sv_structure on a path that did not finish at 10x heartbeats, so a flat netlist was needed even for fdiv16's 111 assigns.

Size: an unrolled f16 SRT16 has 4 iterations, each with a 4-comparator selection stage, two 15-bit CSAs, a 5-way speculative stage (5 x (13-bit CSA + 4 x CSA+adder sign extraction)) and OTFC muxes. That is of the order of 800 to 1200 assigns against the 111 of the fdiv16 reference. Pre-ABC gate count is 12,103, so a pinned-flow score would be several times the reference's 1929.778 GE.

New math with no reuse: SRT radix-4 digit-selection tables (mLookupTable: 4 x 8 constants with 10-bit truncated carry-save estimates), the carry-save residual invariant |w| <= (2/3)d under truncation error, the speculative second selection equalling the true second selection (13-bit estimates, 5 candidate digits), the on-the-fly Q / Q-1 conversion invariants, the final remainder-sign correction, the needShift/oddIter parity mapping, subnormal rounding via fewer iterations, and the modular (W+2)-bit exponent arithmetic including the zeroRes/subRes/infRes thresholds. The restoring-row induction and the M3a-d normalizer of the fdiv16 proof do not apply to SRT. Only the exponent, rounding and special-case certificates (M3e/M3f style) partly carry over.
proofFeasibility.estimate: Fixed-format (5,11), flat rewrite: roughly 3,000 to 6,000 lines of Lean for the math layer, plus a design layer sized like the fdiv16 one (about 1,000 lines) and a sv_equations budget likely 10x the fdiv16 one (that one is 45 s at 600k heartbeats for 111 equations), i.e. several agent-weeks, with finite table checks by kernel decide over about 8 x 2^10 and 8 x 5 x 2^13 cases. Parametric in P adds symbolic LZC/normalizer and induction over the iteration count, roughly doubling it. The fdiv16 reference, at about 1000 lines, is the nearest benchmark.

That means thousands of lines of Lean for a circuit that scores several times worse than the restoring fdiv16 reference. The rewrite is: unroll to combinational (done, 0 mismatches), flatten the 7 multiplier instances, drop `signed`, force NaN sign 0, and add a fixed-format (8,24) task in the style of fdiv16 (kind comb-fixed). The task's parametric statement cannot be proved for W,P other than (8,24), since the design is hard-wired. The statement itself is general, so a (8,24) instance is fine. The math is feasible: the architecture is an exact integer quotient plus remainder followed by textbook RNE, so there is no bounded-ulp approximation to argue around. The one genuinely new obligation compared with fdiv16 is the Newton error bound over all divisors.
blockers: No instances: PROVING.md says sv_structure/sv_equations refuse module instances ('flatten it in the source'). The 7 multiplier uses must be flattened into single-bit assigns, or replaced by something in the fragment.

`*` between two variables is outside the fragment (only + - comparisons and run-time shifts are in). A multiplier has to be a bit-level netlist (the mul task's per-width Dadda references exist, and per-width multiplier proofs there are about 1400 code lines each) or a generate-for shift-and-add chain. My fdiv32_flat.sv uses the shift-add form and extracts cleanly.
`wire signed` and `$signed` (5 declarations) are Unsupported and must be rewritten as unsigned two's-complement arithmetic.
Procedural for loops, casts 5'(i), and used-before-declared must be removed (the priority encoders as ?: chains, which I did).

The Newton error bound: |B*r2 - 2^47| <= 24,992,532 for every one of 2^23 divisors. I measured it exhaustively on the RTL (it equals the generator's stated value), but a Lean proof needs it symbolically. Route: per-interval analysis over the 128 LUT seed buckets (a quadratic error recurrence plus rounding slack), then the deduction rem in [0,16B) with 8-unit bias. Exhaustive kernel `decide` over 8.4M divisors is not realistic, and native_decide adds Lean.ofReduceBool, outside the fdiv16 task's allowed axioms. A fresh fixed-format task could allow it.
The circuit is not minimal-dependency: three different paths (normal, subnormal-grid with m*B, deep flush) must each be tied to the spec's rounding.
proofFeasibility.estimate: Roughly 2,500 to 6,000 lines of Lean in total (fdiv16's reference proof files total about 3,850 lines including its BitVec model and glue). This is an estimate, not a measurement: Newton/residual bound 800 to 1,500, exact-quotient and RNE core with exponent, overflow, subnormal-grid and deep-flush cases 1,000 to 2,000, glue from the netlist equations 500 to 1,000, multiplier lemma (shift-add form) 100 to 300 reused 7 times. sv_equations on a netlist this size (about 25k fine-grained gates after bit-blasting, a few hundred word-level assigns in the shift-add form) is likely the expensive step.

The main new mathematics, with no analogue in fdiv16: the fdiv16 proof closed its numerics by finite certificates (2^32 pairs); here the quotient pairs number 2^46, so an error analysis is needed for 128 seed bins, two fixed-point NR steps with truncation, then the +/-1 residual fix-up. Structure that helps (measured): y2 depends on the divisor only; over all 2^23 divisors e(D)=y2*D-2^50 lies in [-16,793,029, 8,383,406], i.e. |e|<=0.5004*2^25. By my own derivation (not machine-checked) the quotient estimate then satisfies |Qnr - N*2^24/D| <= |e|/2^25 + 1/8 <= 0.6255 < 1 for EVERY dividend N, hence |Qnr - floor| <= 1 and the single +/-1 fix-up gives the exact floor and exact remainder. The divisor-only fact is either an analytic bound (per-bin, the seed is a constant inside a bin so the first step is linear in D) or a kernel decide over 2^23 cases (heavy; native_decide/bv_decide are discouraged and external solvers unsupported).

The shared round/pack stage at 32 bits: denormalizing shift of 0..48 with sticky (49 cases instead of fdiv16's 13), carry into the exponent, overflow threshold, plus the 24-bit clz normalizers and the exponent offset arithmetic; reusable pattern from DpRound but not reusable code.

Statement shape: svGolf's fdiv task is parametric in (W,P) and the checker requires the top module's parameters to match the task's; this design fits only a fixed-size task with W=8,P=24 (like fdiv16 has no parameters), i.e. an `fdiv32` statement over an IEEE-754 binary32 spec function, or a parametric task whose inRange predicate is W=8 /\ P=24.

differences: Only difference, 60 of 4,294,967,296 pairs (MEASURED, exhaustive, all four sign combinations of 15 magnitude pairs): when the exact quotient is the tie 0x3FF.8 ulp (largest subnormal plus half a subnormal ulp = 2047/2^25), RNE must round to even, which is the smallest normal 0x0400, but the design returns +-0 (0x0000 or 0x8000). Example a=0x07ff b=0x4000 got=0x0000 want=0x0400; also a=0x87ff b=0x4000 got=0x8000 want=0x8400; a=0x0bff b=0x4400; a=0x0fff b=0x4800; ... a=0x3fff b=0x7800 (|a| = 0x07ff + 0x400*k, |b| = 0x4000 + 0x400*k, k=0..14). Why only these: for two 11-bit significands a quotient just above the tie cannot occur, so the exact tie is the only way to reach 0x3FF.8 or above.

Mechanism (READ, then confirmed by the patch): after the underflow shift the code sets exp_res = 0. When the rounded significand carries into bit 10 (mant_round = 0x400, mant_round[11] stays 0), the exponent field is taken as exp_res[4:0] = 0 instead of 1, and mant_round[10:0] is nonzero so the zero branch is not taken. Result {sign, 5'd0, 10'd0} = +-0. Patch: add `if ((exp_res == 9'd0) && (mant_round[10] == 1'b1)) exp_field = 5'd1; else` before the existing exp_field selection. Patched file: 0 mismatches over all 2^32 pairs (MEASURED) and 0 over the 4,606,070-pair set vs the Python oracle (MEASURED).

Classes with ZERO mismatches (MEASURED): NaN payload or sign (always 0x7E00), flush-to-zero or denormal handling (subnormal operands and results are exact), inf/zero special cases, overflow and underflow thresholds, rounding other than the one tie, truncation, double rounding, any rounding-mode input (none exists).

Random testing does not find it: 1,000,000 uniform random pairs in my set contain no hit in expectation (60 / 2^32 per pair, about 0.014 expected). Only the structured sweep (every positive finite a times every power-of-two b) found them; the svGolf postsynth corner set (18x18 specials, 4000 random) would not either, but that stage compares ls-sv with the scored netlist, not with the spec, so only the proof can catch it.

runAs: Real design: Verilator 5.042 --cc C++ harness (seq/tb_seq.cpp) on tiny_fp8_unit with the 11 upstream modules unmodified (RD_FIFO_DEPTH=4). It resets, drives issue_valid with opcode 5'b00011 and rm 0, waits for issue_ready, then reads wb_result at wb_valid with wb_ready=1 and records the cycle count. Two modes: isolated (one op at a time) and stream (all 65,536 pairs issued back to back, results collected in order). Combinational variant: comb/fdiv_comb.v, my wrapper that instantiates the unmodified fp8_unpack, fp8_pre_execute, fp8_execute_comb, fp8_normalize and fp8_round with opcode=DIV and rm=000, replacing fp8_div_iter by a 9-stage combinational unroll of its step equations, plus the NaN canonicalizer. Oracle: fdiv_oracle.fdiv(4,4,a,b).

formatsTested.classes: RAW sequential design (real tiny_fp8_unit, opcode 3, rm 0), no wrapper: 6,482 mismatches, all in the NaN payload/sign class (6,474 operand-NaN propagation + 8 invalid-op 0x79), 0 in any other class
after the NaN-to-0x7C wrapper: 0 mismatches for the sequential isolated run, the sequential back-to-back stream run, the combinational unroll in Verilator, and the scored gate netlist of the unroll

conformance: WRAPPER. As shipped, tiny_fp8_unit is a sequential elastic FPU (issue/wb handshake), not a combinational divider, and only (W=4,P=4) exists. Driven through its handshake with opcode DIV (5'b00011) and rm 3'b000 (header ROUND_NEAREST = nearest-even), its output equals the exact oracle on all 65,536 operand pairs except where the oracle result is a NaN: raw output differs from the canonical NaN 0x7C on 6,482 pairs. After the one-line wrapper `is_nan(y) ? 8'h7C : y` it matches on 65,536 of 65,536 pairs, 0 mismatches, in both isolated and back-to-back stream mode. My combinational unroll of the 9 restoring steps (built from the unmodified upstream unpack/pre_execute/execute_comb/normalize/round modules) matches the sequential design bit for bit on all 65,536 pairs, and the pinned-flow gate netlist of that unroll also has 0 mismatches vs the oracle on all 65,536 pairs. Larger or other formats: not supported (all widths hardcoded), so the 2M-random requirement is vacuous; the 8-bit input space was covered exhaustively.
differences: NaN payload/sign (the only functional difference, 6,482 of 65,536 pairs, 0 after wrapper): 6,474 are NaN-operand propagation, where the design returns {sign of the NaN operand, 1111, its payload} instead of 0x7C. Of these, 3,486 have sign bit 1 and 2,988 have sign 0 with payload != 100. 8 are the invalid operations (inf/inf, 0/0 in 4 sign combinations each), where it returns the fixed 0x79 (0_1111_001) instead of 0x7C. 498 propagated NaNs already equal 0x7C. Examples (a,b,got,want): (0x00,0x00,0x79,0x7C), (0x00,0x79,0x79,0x7C). Wrapper: map any NaN result to 8'h7C.
Rounding-mode input: five modes selectable through a 3-bit rm port. rm=3'b000 is round-to-nearest-even and must be pinned by the wrapper. No mismatch once pinned.
Opcode input: the unit has about 21 opcodes (add, sub, mul, div, sqrt, min, max, cvt and others). The wrapper must pin 5'b00011 (DIV).

Not combinational: issue_valid/issue_ready, wb_valid/wb_ready, an rd FIFO, 3 handshake registers and a 1 bit/cycle restoring FSM (fp8_div_iter). Measured latency from the accept edge to wb_valid is exactly 4 cycles for special-case operands (8,892 pairs) and exactly 14 cycles for real finite/finite divides (56,644 pairs). Back-to-back throughput is 9.64 cycles/op averaged over all pairs. Extra outputs (flags, exceptions, rd) are unused.

Format coverage: only (W=4,P=4), i.e. 1 sign, 4 exponent bits with bias 7, 3 fraction bits and IEEE-style inf/NaN at exponent 1111. Widths are hardcoded literals (4'b1111, 6'sd7, mA4/mB4, QDIV=5), so it is not parametric. The header's WIDTH/EXP_WIDTH/MANT_WIDTH macros do not drive the datapath.
No mismatch found in: inf/zero special cases and their signs, flush-to-zero (none, subnormals are exact), double rounding, exponent overflow/underflow thresholds, subnormal results.
wrapperNeeded: Sequential original: (1) drive the handshake (issue_valid with issue_opcode=5'b00011, issue_rm=3'b000, issue_rd any, wb_ready=1, flush=0), wait 4 to 14 cycles for wb_valid, read wb_result. (2) Canonicalize NaNs: q = (q[6:3]==4'hF && q[2:0]!=0) ? 8'h7C : q. For svGolf's combinational port list a,b,q, a combinational unroll of the 9 restoring steps is needed (mine: comb/fdiv_comb.v, same step equations, verified equal to the FSM on all 65,536 pairs), plus a macro/include expansion pass. The source gate refuses `include and every `define use (24 findings on fp8_round.v alone), but passes the flat text after `verilator -E` with the `line markers stripped (comb/pre/fdiv_comb_pp.sv).

proofFeasibility.judgement: Provable after a stated rewrite; not as is. The divider is real, exact and tiny, and only needs a fixed-size task at (4,4) (design/fdiv-param option C, a family of fixed-size tasks, needs no change to Task.lean). Neither the shipped RTL nor my hierarchical unroll is in the tactic fragment. The proof is for a hand-flattened, DIV-only, RNE-only, combinational rewrite with the NaN canonicalizer folded in. The sequential original would need the repository's sequential layer and is not provable through the combinational interface.
proofFeasibility.estimate: All of this is an estimate, none measured (Lean was not run). Rewrite: about 100 to 150 lines of flat SV, with all sites plain (no generate, no always_comb, per H2-NOTE G5). It would cover: classification and specials; subnormal pre-normalize by a 3-way priority; a 9-step restoring chain written out flat; the msb of the 6-bit quotient (only bits 5 or 4 can be the msb, so no priority-encoder loop is needed); and the exponent difference, with the subnormal right shift and the RNE round-up and overflow, all in unsigned two's-complement. Proof: roughly 300 to 700 lines of Lean. A naive single exhaustive `decide +kernel` over 65,536 pairs, scaled from aes_sbox (10.5 s for 256 inputs of a 113-site packed program), would come to roughly 45 to 90 minutes. That is far over the 130 to 400 s limits of existing tasks, so the proof should be decomposed. The pieces: specials by classification case split; the 8x8 significand pairs against the format-agnostic restore_spec in SpecFacts.lean; and normalize/round as a finite case table, linked to the spec via the format-agnostic certificate (certF_bridge / fdivF_cert in CertF.lean). By comparison, fdiv16 took about 1000 lines of math, and the parametric statement needs none of it for a fixed format.

Extractor-unsupported constructs: signed arithmetic, procedural for loop (also refused by fourstate as a run-time index mag[i]), user function do_round, localparam signed with width conversion, unpacked arrays and wire initializers in the unroll.
Fragment restrictions from H2-NOTE: the 9-stage chain must be written flat, with no concatenation as a ?: arm or +,-,>= operand, and no operation as the left operand of a shift (name it first).

The spec wants 0x7C for every NaN result, but upstream returns 0x79 for invalid operations and a propagated payload and sign for NaN operands: the rewrite must canonicalize, so it is no longer upstream code.

verdict: WRAPPER, one small format. It is exact for the spec at (W=4,P=4): 0 mismatches over all 65,536 pairs, after pinning opcode=DIV and rm=RNE and mapping every NaN to 0x7C, which fixes the only difference (6,482 NaN payload/sign pairs). It adds a new cheap (W,P) point and an exhaustively checkable independent algorithm. The shipped design is a sequential 21-opcode FPU, not a divider: 4/14-cycle latency, 199 flip-flops. Only my combinational unroll is scoreable, at 542.271 GE / depth 63. As submitted it cannot be proved: a flat DIV-only rewrite and a fixed-size (4,4) task statement are needed, and the proof would be moderate work. A useful data point, but not a general-purpose candidate: not parametric and no larger format.
